title: Autoscale Workbench: interactive policy editor, throughput preview, and immutable change log
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description: Goal: Ship an Autoscale Workbench inside Console that merges a policy editor, a throughput preview/simulator, and an immutable change log so operators can author autoscale policies with confidence and auditability. This ticket covers the PM scope: requirements, acceptance criteria, stakeholder alignment, rollout plan, and signoff. The workbench should enable operators to: (1) create/modify autoscaling policies (min/max capacity, target throughput, target latency or cost objective, cooldowns), (2) run a historical workload simulation to preview expected capacity, cost, and SLO impact, (3) view per-fleet throughput dashboards (token/s, requests/s, p50/p95 latency, queue depth) inline while editing, and (4) see an immutable change log with author, diff, rationale, and a one-click revert option. Key constraints: must not expose controls that can immediately scale to >2x reserved capacity without a two-step approval; apply RBAC checks and record KMS-backed audit events for Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscale policy editor UI with fields: min_instances, max_instances, target_tokens_per_sec, target_p95_latency_ms, cooldown_seconds, scaling_window_minutes
Inline throughput preview that runs a dry-run against the last 72h of anonymized workload and shows estimated token/sec, estimated cost delta, and expected latency changes
Throughput dashboard embedded in workbench showing live and historical token/sec, requests/sec, p50/p95 latency, and batching efficiency; charts link to Grafana panel
Immutable change log: records who changed what, timestamp, textual diff, ability to add rationale, tie to GitHub PR or runbook, and revert to previous policy with optional canary rollout
RBAC gating: only users with fleet-admin role can publish changes; others can draft and request approval
Security review completed and audit events emitted for policy publishes in Private deployments
E2E tests covering editor validation, preview job scheduling, and revert workflow; UI smoke tests for dashboard rendering
Performance: preview run completes within 30s for 72h sample on typical customer fleet (approx 10K requests/day)
qa_notes: Use staging fleet with synthetic workload generator (loadgen v2) to validate preview accuracy
Verify RBAC by testing roles: fleet-viewer, fleet-editor, fleet-admin across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
Confirm audit events appear in customer audit log with encryption metadata for Private deployments
rollout_plan: Alpha behind feature-flag for internal SRE and 3 pilot customers (week 1)
Collect pilot feedback, adjust simulator defaults and cost model (week 2)
Gradual rollout to 25% accounts on Hosted with telemetry gating; Dedicated opt-in; Private via controlled upgrade (weeks 3-4)
Enable revert-by-default and a 24h auto-rollback safety window for first 2 weeks
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Chose historical-simulation approach over model-based prediction after SRE workshop (reason: higher operator trust and reproducibility)
2026-03-02: Agreed to limit immediate-scaling factor to 2x without approval; documented in policy constraints
2026-03-08: Decided to surface cost delta in estimated USD and normalized tokens/unit for cross-customer comparability
tradeoffs: Simulator accuracy vs latency: we cap historical window to 72h to keep preview runs under 30s; long-window analysis reserved for offline reports
Complexity vs transparency: chose simple, explainable heuristics rather than an opaque ML predictor for initial launch
UI density vs clarity: dashboards embedded in workbench reduce context switching but increase page load; implemented lazy-loading of charts
